patience.title: Terminal Patience
patience.help: Each wire colour goes onto its busbar in ascending order from 0.5 to 25 mm². In the cable duct a terminal only takes the next smaller cross-section of the other colour group (dark: brown, black – light: grey, blue). Two spare slots hold one terminal each. Click a terminal, then a target; double-click puts it on the rail.

publish.title: Publish as job
publish.intro: Define how it is verified: the operating sequence of buttons and switches, and rules that must hold. Your own solution must pass the job; its metrics become the reference values.

coach.finishedText: Your plant runs with your program. Next: sort workpieces – the templates under “More → My plants” show how. The introduction is always available under “More”.

savegame.offerTitle: Take over the save game from the web version?
savegame.offerText: If you have already played in the browser: save the file spielstand-export.json there via “Save game → Export everything” in the inbox and choose it here. You can also do this later from the “Save game” menu.
block.protected: Protected block: the code cannot be viewed or changed. You use it through its interface.
cabinet.hscHint: Counts every rising edge at channel 0 independently of the cycle. Count as DInt in the input area, bit 0 of the same byte in the output area resets it (e.g. %ID112 / %Q112.0).
cabinet.pulseHint: One control word per channel (2 bytes): PWM duty cycle in per mille (0…1000), PTO frequency in Hz (0…500).
cabinet.controllerHint: The modules of this station belong to this CPU; their addresses continue after the CPU's own modules.
cabinet.updateHint: How often the station exchanges inputs and outputs with the CPU – extra delay compared to central I/O.
cabinet.connHint: Connections for TSEND_C/TRCV_C: both CPUs use the same ID.

language.label: Language
mail.subject: Subject
block.tpaHint: Process image partition: the interrupt OB reads its partition's inputs before it starts and writes its outputs afterwards. Without a partition it only works through the OB1 process image.
cabinet.tpaHint: Channels in a process image partition are only updated by the interrupt OB with that partition, not by OB1. Once any module has a partition, interrupt OBs without one no longer read or write I/O.
graph.initialHint: The chain starts with this step after startup
graph.removeStep: Delete the step and its transitions
graph.hint: A transition switches at most once per cycle; if a step has several outgoing transitions, the first one that is true wins (alternative branch). In conditions “Schrittzeit” stands for the time since the step became active. N and D only apply in the active step, S and R store.
hmi.ackHint: Acknowledge all new alarms; in the program the alarm's Ack_State becomes TRUE
hmi.addressesHint: Memory addresses of the panel elements (bit e.g. %M200.0, word e.g. %MW220); empty = automatic
library.sameName: own block with the same name
scenario.title: Scenarios
scenario.empty: No scenario yet. A scenario is a test run with a timeline: operation, faults, power failure, inserted parts and levels at fixed or random times – plus rules that must hold. “+ New” creates one.
scenario.name: Name
scenario.missing: Refers to parts that no longer exist: {refs}
scenario.eventsHint: Time in s; “+” shifts the event randomly per seed by up to that many seconds. Events at 0 s set the initial state.
scenario.jitterTitle: Random offset: per seed the event comes up to that many seconds later
scenario.label: Scenario
random.title: Random jobs
random.intro: Every random job is rolled from a blueprint and verified with a reference solution before it is handed out – so it can be solved. The code (e.g. SGN-4K7Q2M) gives the same job everywhere: to share or compare.
random.badCode: That is not a valid job code (form: SGN-4K7Q2M).
random.busy: Generating job {code} and verifying it with the reference solution …
random.deleteConfirm: Delete random job {code}? It can be generated again from the code at any time.
course.title: Basics course
course.hint: For beginners without PLC experience: the basics from scratch
course.quizFirst: First answer the questions above correctly.
start.title: How would you like to start?
start.beginnerText: The basics course explains everything from scratch: signals, logic, timers, counters, step sequences. Afterwards job 0 guides you with detailed hints.
start.proText: Start right away with job 0 and the short step card. The basics course stays available via 🎓 at any time.

monitor.title: Monitoring on/off: while the simulation runs, current values are shown right in the program – SCL to the right of each line, FBD/LAD at pins and wires (green = 1 or power, blue = 0).
monitor.startSim: Start the simulation to see values
monitor.noInstance: No instance DB – local values not visible
graph.faultIn: Fault in step {no} – acknowledge with ACK_EF
graph.interlockHint: C – interlock: the actions of the step only take effect while the condition holds; otherwise fault (ERR_FLT).
graph.supervisionHint: V – supervision: if the condition becomes true, the step reports a fault and the sequence does not advance until acknowledged with ACK_EF.
graph.targetHint: Target step(s): one number, or several ("3, 4") for a simultaneous branch – all become active at once.
graph.joinHint: Synchronisation: further steps that must be active too ("5, 7") – the transition only switches when all are active.
graph.paramsHint: The sequence FB also has the parameters OFF_SQ, INIT_SQ, ACK_EF, SW_AUTO/SW_TAP/SW_MAN, T_PUSH, S_SEL/S_ON (inputs) and ERR_FLT, S_NO, AUTO_ON/TAP_ON/MAN_ON (outputs), e.g. "Bohren_DB"(ACK_EF := "Quittieren");
diag.offline: Start the simulation to see the state of the CPU and the modules.
